Full Release

GEORGE TOWN, Cayman Islands, Nov. 09, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Consolidated Water Co. Ltd . (NASDAQ Global Select Market: CWCO), a leading designer, builder and operator of advanced water treatment plants, reported results for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026. All comparisons are to the same prior-year period unless otherwise noted.

Consolidated Water will hold a conference call at 11:00 a.m. Eastern time tomorrow to discuss the results (see dial-in information below).

Third Quarter 2026 Financial Summary

  • Total revenue decreased 11.9% to $30.9 million from $35.1 million, due to lower services and manufacturing revenue, partially offset by increases in retail and bulk revenue.
  • Retail revenue increased 5.7% to $8.2 million, principally due to higher energy pass-through charges and an increased rate for a major commercial customer, offsetting lower retail rates under the new license.
  • Bulk revenue increased 20.8% to $10.1 million, principally due to higher energy pass-through charges and, to a lesser extent, revenue from the new Cat Island, Bahamas desalination plants.
  • Manufacturing revenue decreased 39.7% to $2.8 million due to a decrease in the total dollar amount of contracts completed and in progress.
  • Services revenue decreased 31.7% to $9.8 million. Construction revenue declined to $3.5 million from $6.4 million. Recurring operations and maintenance (O&M) revenue decreased to $6.1 million from $7.7 million, primarily due to the expiration of contracts with three customers in California in the first quarter of 2026.
  • Net income from continuing operations attributable to company stockholders totaled $2.4 million or $0.15 per diluted share, compared to $5.6 million or $0.34 per diluted share in the third quarter of 2025.
  • Including discontinued operations, net income attributable to company stockholders totaled $2.3 million or $0.14 per diluted share, compared to $5.5 million or $0.34 per diluted share in the third quarter of 2025.
  • Cash and cash equivalents totaled $129.2 million and working capital was $145.1 million as of September 30, 2026.

Third Quarter 2026 Operational Summary

  • Cayman Water’s new 25-year retail water license became effective August 1, 2026, establishing a long-term regulatory framework and preserving the company’s exclusive right to produce, distribute and sell potable water within its licensed service area in Grand Cayman, Cayman Islands.
  • Received approximately $10.1 million in purchase orders from a municipality on Florida’s east coast to design, fabricate and deliver nanofiltration membrane water treatment equipment and horizontal cartridge filters. These represent the company’s largest municipal membrane-based water treatment equipment and horizontal cartridge filter orders to date. Delivery is scheduled for November 2027.
  • Advanced the Hawaii seawater desalination project. In July 2026, the Honolulu Board of Water Supply issued a Limited Notice to Proceed releasing approximately $6 million for long-lead equipment procurement.

Management Commentary

“Increases to our third-quarter retail and bulk revenue were offset by lower construction, O&M and manufacturing revenue,” said Consolidated Water CEO Rick McTaggart.

“Cayman Water’s new 25-year retail license, effective August 1, 2026, establishes a long-term regulatory framework and provides exclusive rights within our licensed service area. The new rate structure lowers base rates for customers and retains an annual water rate adjustment mechanism, subject to regulatory verification and approval. Although lower retail rates reduced quarterly retail gross profit, higher energy pass-through charges, a 1% increase in water sales volume, and an increased rate for a major commercial customer increased retail revenue.

“Our bulk segment revenue increased primarily from higher energy pass-through charges and, to a lesser extent, revenue from our new Cat Island, Bahamas desalination plants. Bulk gross profit increased, but higher diesel costs and incremental maintenance expenses reduced gross margin as a percentage of revenue.

“Manufacturing revenue declined as the total dollar amount of contracts completed and in progress decreased. Based on current projections, we continue to expect full-year 2026 manufacturing revenue to be below 2025 levels. However, during the quarter we announced approximately $10.1 million in purchase orders from a municipality on Florida’s east coast for nanofiltration membrane water treatment equipment and horizontal cartridge filters for delivery in November 2027. These orders, which are our largest municipal membrane equipment and horizontal cartridge filter orders to date, demonstrate the breadth of our manufacturing capabilities.

“Additionally, we have bid for water equipment manufacturing projects valued at approximately $10 million that are expected to be decided and awarded in the fourth quarter of this year and are tracking approximately $45 million in Florida municipal water projects that are expected to go out for bid within the next six months. Our excellent reputation, world-class manufacturing capabilities, and deep knowledge of the Florida water equipment market should help us be very competitive on these new opportunities. All of this bodes well for a strong 2027 for our manufacturing business.

“After quarter-end, we announced on October 12 that we had been awarded an approximately $39.8 million design-build agreement by the City of Pismo Beach, California, for the Central Coast Blue Advanced Water Purification Facility. We were selected through a competitive procurement process to design, construct, and test the facility, train City personnel and support initial operations. The project is intended to provide a new local, drought-resistant water supply and help protect the groundwater basin from seawater intrusion. Construction is anticipated to begin in spring 2027, with design, permitting, construction, startup and commissioning expected to span approximately 24 months overall.

“In Hawaii, the July Limited Notice to Proceed authorized approximately $6 million for critical long-lead equipment for our planned Kalaeloa desalination facility. Early procurement should help reduce scheduling pressure and position us to advance construction efficiently once the remaining permits and approvals are secured.

“Design and construction of the Hawaii project represents more than $150 million of contracted backlog which has not yet been recognized as revenue. Once construction of this project commences in the first half of 2027, we expect it to have a significant impact on our revenue and earnings. Recent approvals from the State Historic Preservation Division and the Hawaii Department of Health allow us to pursue remaining permits and approvals. The Honolulu Board of Water Supply remains supportive and has granted schedule extensions to reflect the permitting process. We anticipate beginning construction in the first half of 2027, subject to obtaining the remaining permits and approvals. Following commissioning, we are contracted to operate and maintain the Kalaeloa facility for 20 years, with two additional five-year extension options at the client’s discretion.

“Looking ahead, we remain focused on executing our projects, serving our customers and pursuing opportunities that build on our water-treatment expertise. We believe our diversified business and disciplined approach to growth provide a solid foundation for the future. Our priority remains translating these strengths into sustainable long-term growth and enhanced shareholder value.”

Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results

Revenue totaled $30.9 million, decreasing 11.9% from $35.1 million in the third quarter of 2025. The decrease reflected lower services and manufacturing revenue, partially offset by increased retail and bulk revenue.

Retail revenue increased 5.7% to $8.2 million from $7.8 million, principally due to higher pass-through energy charges and an increased rate for a major commercial water customer. These factors offset the impact of lower retail water rates effective August 1, 2026, under the new retail license. Water sales volume increased approximately 1%.

Bulk revenue increased 20.8% to $10.1 million from $8.4 million, principally due to higher pass-through energy charges at CW-Bahamas and, to a lesser extent, revenue from its new Cat Island plants.

Services revenue decreased 31.7% to $9.8 million from $14.3 million. Construction revenue declined to $3.5 million from $6.4 million due to a decrease in the number and total value of construction projects. O&M revenue decreased to $6.1 million from $7.7 million, primarily due to the expiration of contracts with three customers in California in the first quarter of 2026. Design and consulting revenue was $177,000 compared to $214,000.

Manufacturing revenue decreased 39.7% to $2.8 million from $4.7 million due to a decrease in the total dollar amount of contracts completed and in progress. The company expects full-year 2026 manufacturing revenue to be below 2025 levels based on current projections.

Gross profit for the third quarter of 2026 was $9.8 million (31.8% of total revenue), compared to $12.9 million (36.9% of total revenue) in the third quarter of 2025.

Net income from continuing operations attributable to Consolidated Water stockholders for the third quarter of 2026 was $2.4 million or $0.15 per diluted share, compared to $5.6 million or $0.34 per diluted share in the third quarter of 2025.

Including discontinued operations, net income attributable to Consolidated Water stockholders for the third quarter of 2026 was $2.3 million or $0.14 per diluted share, compared to $5.5 million or $0.34 per diluted share in the third quarter of 2025.

As of September 30, 2026, cash and cash equivalents totaled $129.2 million, working capital was $145.1 million, and equity attributable to Consolidated Water stockholders was $226.2 million.

First Nine Months 2026 Financial Results

Revenue for the first nine months of 2026 was $93.8 million, down 8.5% from $102.4 million in the same year-ago period. Manufacturing revenue decreased by $8.8 million, services revenue decreased by $3.2 million, and retail revenue decreased by $0.4 million. These decreases were partially offset by a $3.7 million increase in bulk revenue.

Retail revenue decreased to $25.4 million from $25.8 million, reflecting a 4.1% decrease in water sales volume. The decrease in volume was attributable to significantly greater rainfall on Grand Cayman in 2026 compared to 2025, when rainfall was well below historical norms.

Bulk revenue increased 14.9% to $28.8 million from $25.1 million, principally due to higher pass-through energy charges at CW-Bahamas and, to a lesser extent, revenue from its new Cat Island plants.

Services revenue decreased 9.0% to $32.6 million from $35.8 million. Construction revenue was $10.9 million compared to $11.4 million in the same year-ago period. O&M revenue decreased 11.2% to $21.0 million from $23.7 million due to the expiration of contracts with three customers in California in the first quarter of 2026. Design and consulting revenue was $642,000 compared to $716,000.

Manufacturing revenue decreased 56.1% to $6.9 million from $15.7 million due to a decrease in the total dollar amount of contracts completed and in progress.

Gross profit for the first nine months of 2026 was $31.7 million (33.8% of total revenue), down 16.8% from $38.1 million (37.2% of total revenue) in the same year-ago period.

Net income from continuing operations attributable to Consolidated Water stockholders for the first nine months of 2026 was $10.2 million or $0.64 per diluted share, compared to $15.7 million or $0.97 per diluted share for the first nine months of 2025.

Including discontinued operations, net income attributable to Consolidated Water stockholders for the first nine months of 2026 was $10.0 million or $0.62 per diluted share, compared to $15.4 million or $0.96 per diluted share in the same period of 2025.

SANTA ANA, Calif., Nov. 09, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- INVE Technologies, Inc. (NASDAQ: INVE) (the “Company”) today announced that it has entered into a definitive strategic partnership agreement with Trackonomy Systems, Inc. (“Trackonomy”). The agreement formalizes the commercial framework established between the companies to deploy Trackonomy’s physical AI platform across enterprise software businesses acquired by INVE Technologies.

Under the agreement, INVE Technologies anticipates incorporating Trackonomy’s physical AI infrastructure and Sentient platform into its acquired software products. This integration will create a structured data layer using verified real-world operational inputs, enabling the Company’s acquired SaaS businesses to launch premium physical AI offerings designed to expand contract values and improve operating margins.

The agreement establishes commercial terms governing preferential pricing, software licensing, and revenue sharing across jointly offered solutions. INVE Technologies will serve as a preferred reseller of Trackonomy’s physical AI solutions, including sensors, smart Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) labels, RFID hardware, and its Sentient platform. In turn, Trackonomy will provide the underlying infrastructure, install hardware at customer sites, and assist in porting software applications onto its platform, accelerating Trackonomy’s distribution into established SaaS customer accounts across regulated industries.

“This strategic partnership aligns our physical AI strategy directly with Trackonomy’s technology,” said James Greenwell, Interim CEO of INVE Technologies. “Working together, we can pursue new enterprise software opportunities that deliver the verifiable ground-truth data increasingly required by customers and regulators.”

“Through this strategic partnership with INVE Technologies, we believe Trackonomy will further enhance its position as a global provider of vertically integrated physical AI solutions across multiple industries,” added Dr. Erik Volkerink, Co-Founder and CEO of Trackonomy.

INVE Technologies’ acquisition strategy focuses on established software platforms in highly regulated markets, including healthcare, pharmaceutical logistics, food safety, environmental monitoring, and worker safety (EHS). Acquired SaaS companies are expected to retain their customer relationships and brand identities while INVE Technologies centralizes corporate overhead, finance, and legal administration.

In addition, INVE Technologies holds a preferred equity position in Trackonomy, and both companies maintain reciprocal non-voting board observer seats that are currently held by INVE Technologies Chairman James E. Ousley and Trackonomy CEO Dr. Erik Volkerink.

About INVE Technologies
INVE Technologies is a publicly traded operating company focused on acquiring and operating enterprise-enabled intelligent software businesses serving highly regulated industries. Its strategy is to combine established enterprise SaaS platforms with Physical AI capabilities to support automated, continuous, and verifiable operational data. For additional information, visit invetechnologies.com .

About Trackonomy
Trackonomy is a San Jose, California-based Physical AI company and the only one spanning the full stack through three independent businesses: InPlay (chips for manufacturers and IoT companies), Identiv (smart labels for IoT companies and end customers), and Sentient (end-to-end solutions for end customers). Trackonomy pioneered the smart label category nearly a decade ago and leads it today, holding the industry’s broadest patent portfolio and orchestrating over 20 million shipments daily across logistics, aviation, healthcare, defense, and retail. A World Economic Forum Technology Pioneer with over 500 employees, three factories, and five R&D centers on three continents, Trackonomy has raised over $250 million from investors including 8VC, Kleiner Perkins, Koch Disruptive Technologies, and In-Q-Tel. Learn more at Trackonomy.ai .

(NASDAQ: ORRF) (the “Company”), the holding company of Orrstown Bank (the “Bank”), today announced the execution of a strategic repositioning of a portion of its available for sale (“AFS”) securities portfolio. Full Release

HOUSTON, Nov. 09, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Microvast Holdings, Inc. (NASDAQ:MVST) (“Microvast” or the “Company”), today announced its unaudited consolidated financial results for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 (“Q3 2026”).

“The third quarter presented a highly challenging operating environment as we navigated softer commercial vehicle demand across our key markets in Europe and APAC, compounded by ongoing industry pricing pressures,” said Yang Wu, Microvast’s Founder, Chairman, and Chief Executive Officer. The material decline in sales, gross margin and operating performance during the quarter have significantly constrained our liquidity. Considering our current balance sheet position, our focus is on the actions within our control: reducing costs, preserving liquidity, and negotiating with our lenders in an attempt to refinance, extend or restructure our near-term debt obligations. Regarding our current operations, installation and commissioning of our Huzhou Phase 3.2 production equipment have been completed and the pack assembly line at our Clarksville facility is substantially completed. We recognize that the outcome of these efforts is uncertain and depends on factors outside our control, including lender decisions and customer demand.”

Q3 2026 Results

  • Revenues of $45.8 million, compared to $123.3 million in Q3 2025, decreasing by $77.5 million, or 62.8%. The decrease was primarily driven by a 62.2% reduction in sales volume from approximately 501.7 MWh in Q3 2025 to approximately 189.6 MWh in Q3 2026. The decline reflected weaker sales across Europe and APAC as the result of softer end-market demand for heavy-duty trucks, port equipment, and heavy mining equipment, which led to reduced orders from several of our long-standing customers across Europe and APAC. Demand continued to be adversely affected by evolving commercial vehicle regulatory and geopolitical dynamics, including the Indian and Korean markets, and demand shift towards lower cost products in India. The decrease in U.S. sales versus the prior year period was primarily due to our largest customer bringing product into 2025 as a result of uncertainty around tariff outcomes.
  • Gross margin decreased to 5.2% from 37.6% in Q3 2025. This change was primarily attributable to a $9.3 million write-down for obsolete inventories related to specialized energy storage system (“ESS”) components and other inventories, which negatively impacted our gross margin by 20.4 percentage points. Excluding the impact of this non-cash charge, the decreased gross margin reflected the significant reduction in sales volume, and continued pricing pressure in the lithium battery industry. The decrease in revenue also reduced the absorption of fixed manufacturing and operating costs, further compressing gross margin.
  • Operating expenses increased to $69.0 million, compared to $31.6 million in Q3 2025. This increase in operating expenses was primarily driven by non-cash impairment charges of long-lived assets of $35.7 million, including a $15.0 million, $4.4 million, and $16.3 million impairment loss for our operations in China, Germany, and the U.S., respectively. The impairment charges resulted from impairment testing of all production line assets and construction-in-progress assets, triggered by a material decline in sales, gross margin, and operating performance during Q3 2026.
  • Net loss of $76.8 million, compared to net loss of $1.5 million in Q3 2025. The increase in net loss was primarily attributable to the $35.7 million non-cash impairment charges of long-lived assets and lower gross profit on reduced revenue in the quarter. Non-GAAP adjusted net loss* was $76.0 million, compared to non-GAAP adjusted net profit* of $11.9 million in Q3 2025.
  • Net loss per share of $0.20, compared to net loss per share of $0.00 in Q3 2025. Non-GAAP adjusted net loss per share* was $0.20, compared to non-GAAP adjusted net profit per share* of $0.04 in Q3 2025.
  • Non-GAAP adjusted EBITDA* of negative $60.8 million in Q3 2026, compared to non-GAAP adjusted EBITDA* of $21.9 million in Q3 2025.
  • Capital expenditures of $2.3 million, compared to $17.4 million in Q3 2025.
  • Cash, cash equivalents and restricted cash of $124.4 million as of September 30, 2026, compared to $169.2 million as of December 31, 2025, and $142.6 million as of September 30, 2025.

Nine Months Ended September 30, 2026 Results (“YTD 2026”)

  • Revenues of $193.7 million compared to $331.1 million in the nine months ended September 30, 2025 (“YTD 2025”), a decrease of 41.5%. The decrease was primarily driven by a 37.4% reduction in sales volume, which reflected weaker sales across Europe and APAC as the result of softer end-market demand for heavy-duty trucks, port equipment, and heavy mining equipment, which led to reduced orders from several of our long-standing customers, across Europe and APAC, and a $2.7 million IEEPA (1) tariff refund issued to a customer recorded as a reduction to our revenue in the current period.
  • Gross margin decreased to 24.4% from 36.6% in YTD 2025. This change was primarily attributable to an $11.1 million write-down for obsolete inventories related to specialized ESS components and other inventories, which negatively impacted our gross margin by 5.7 percentage points. Excluding the impact of this non-cash charge, the decreased gross margin reflected the significant reduction in sales volume, changes in geographic markets, continued pricing pressure in the lithium battery industry higher raw material prices, and lower production utilization, which reduced fixed cost absorption, slightly offset by the recognition of IEEPA (1) tariff refunds received.
  • Operating expenses increased to $123.6 million, compared to $84.4 million in YTD 2025. This increase in operating expenses was primarily driven by non-cash impairment charges of long-lived assets of $35.8 million.
  • Net loss of $40.6 million, compared to net loss of $45.8 million in YTD 2025. The decrease in net loss was primarily attributable to a $58.0 million non-cash gain from the change in fair value of the warrant liability prior to their expiration on July 23, 2026 and convertible loan prior to its settlement on May 28, 2026, compared to a $91.0 million non-cash loss in YTD 2025, partially offset by the $35.8 million non-cash impairment of long-lived assets, lower gross profit, a $15.4 million foreign exchange loss compared to a $9.0 million foreign exchange gain in YTD 2025, $5.4 million of income tax expense resulting from a full valuation allowance against our deferred tax assets. Non-GAAP adjusted net loss* was $96.0 million, compared to non-GAAP adjusted net profit of $47.5 million in YTD 2025.
  • Net loss per share of $0.11, compared to net loss per share of $0.14 in YTD 2025. Non-GAAP adjusted net loss per share* was $0.27, compared to non-GAAP adjusted net profit per share* of $0.15 in YTD 2025.
  • Non-GAAP adjusted EBITDA* of negative $62.7 million in YTD 2026, compared to non-GAAP adjusted EBITDA* of $76.3 million in YTD 2025.
  • Capital expenditures of $17.9 million, compared to $31.4 million in YTD 2025.

*The Company presents its financial results in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles in the United States of America (“GAAP”). However, management believes that using additional non-GAAP measures will enhance the evaluation of the profitability of the Company and its ongoing operations. Please see the tables on pages 14-17 below for reconciliations of GAAP to non-GAAP financial measures. The Consolidated Balance Sheets, Consolidated Statements of Operations, and Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows are derived from the consolidated financial statements presented in our Quarterly Report on Form 10-Q as of and for the three- and nine-month periods ended September 30, 2026.

(1) In February 2026, the United States Supreme Court ruled that certain tariffs imposed under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act (“IEEPA”) were not authorized by statute. Following the ruling, the U.S. Court of International Trade ordered U.S. Customs and Border Protection to suspend collection of such tariffs and to establish a process to refund amounts previously collected. As a result of this ruling, the Company is eligible to receive refunds of tariffs previously paid on qualifying imports. During the nine months ended September 30, 2026, the Company received $4.4 million in tariff refunds, excluding interest. Of this amount, $2.7 million was issued in tariff refunds to a customer. The IEEPA tariff refunds received were recognized as a reduction to the cost of revenue, while the refund issued to our customer was recognized as a reduction of revenue for the nine months ended September 30, 2026.

Liquidity and Balance Sheet

  • Cash, cash equivalents and restricted cash totaled $124.4 million as of September 30, 2026, of which $84.8 million was comprised of cash and cash equivalents. Of the cash and cash equivalents, $30.4 million was held by our Chinese subsidiaries and $14.4 million was held by our European subsidiaries. Due to foreign regulatory restrictions, adverse tax consequences and localized working capital needs, we are currently unable to repatriate cash from China and Europe to fund our U.S. operations. We currently intend to retain available funds and any future earnings to satisfy our debt obligations and to support ongoing operations in China, Europe and the U.S.
  • Net cash used in our operating activities was $65.4 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $59.5 million in cash generated by operating activities in the same period in 2025.
  • Total debt was $177.0 million as of September 30, 2026, consisting of $135.3 million of bank borrowings and $41.7 million of convertible bonds issued by Microvast Power Systems Co., Ltd. (“MPS”), our principal operating subsidiary in China, to Huzhou Saiyuan. Current bank borrowings, notes payable and current bonds payable totaled approximately $196.0 million, and we had a working capital deficit of $3.1 million.
  • As of the date of this release, our near-term debt obligations include: (i) $41.7 million of convertible bonds, due, together with accrued interest, on or before January 31, 2027; (ii) $84.0 million of short-term bank loans of our PRC subsidiaries, which mature at various dates during the next twelve months; and (iii) $373 thousand, $149 thousand, $13.8 million and $149 thousand of principal under MPS’s long-term working capital loans, due December 19, 2026, March 18, 2027, June 19, 2027 and September 18, 2027, respectively. Our ability to make these payments depends on our ability to refinance or extend these obligations. We are in ongoing negotiations with our lenders regarding these obligations, but there can be no assurance that these obligations will be refinanced or extended on acceptable terms, or at all. A failure to make any of these payments will result in an event of default and the acceleration of substantially all of our bank borrowings and bonds payable and the enforcement of security over MPS’s assets and our equity interest in MPS. As of September 30, 2026, we also had outstanding borrowings of $22.4 million under our loan facilities agreement entered into on September 27, 2022 with a group of lenders led by a bank in China, which were due on December 10, 2026. Subsequent to September 30, 2026, we repaid the remaining balance of $22.4 million, and that facility was fully repaid and retired. Additionally, during the nine months ended September 30, 2026, we secured $95.8 million of bank borrowings, of which $59.8 million represented refinanced debt, and since September 30, 2026, we have refinanced an additional $8.9 million of short-term bank borrowings.
  • As of October 31, 2026, our total usable cash across all of our entities was approximately $71.3 million. Based on our current forecasts, absent additional financing, the refinancing or extension of our debt obligations, or further cost reductions, we expect our available cash to be insufficient to meet our obligations as they come due over the next twelve months, including our near-term debt maturities and pending legal settlements.
  • Our revenues are materially concentrated with a small number of customers, and there is significant uncertainty regarding the level of future orders from certain of our largest customers. One of our significant European customers was recently acquired by a third party, which creates additional uncertainty regarding its future purchases from us. We currently have limited visibility into our revenue for the next several quarters and into cash collections in the near term, and our first quarter has historically reflected nominal reductions in activity related to the Chinese New Year holiday.

Going Concern

Based on our current cash flow forecasts, absent additional financing, the refinancing, extension or restructuring of our debt obligations, or significant further reductions in costs, we expect our available cash to be insufficient to meet our obligations as they come due over the next twelve months. Management has concluded that its plans to alleviate the substantial doubt about our ability to continue as a going concern cannot be deemed probable of being effectively implemented and, accordingly, the substantial doubt has not been alleviated.

2026 Outlook

In light of the uncertainty regarding our liquidity position, our ongoing discussions with our lenders regarding the refinancing, extension or restructuring of our near-term debt obligations, and softer end-market demand, we are implementing operating cost reduction initiatives across all areas of the business, reducing or deferring certain discretionary capital expenditures and implementing targeted reductions in workforce in certain of our operations. Our cost-reduction program has not been fully implemented, and the cash costs associated with these actions have strained and may continue to strain our near-term liquidity.

  • We continue to explore potential opportunities in the commercial vehicle market.
  • Installation and commissioning of the Phase 3.2 production equipment at our Huzhou, China facility have been completed. Production ramp-up is dependent on customer demand, production yields, product qualification, operating efficiency and working capital availability. Unless production volumes increase sufficiently, the Phase 3.2 line will operate below its designed capacity.
  • The pack assembly line at our Clarksville facility is substantially completed. Resumption of full-scale construction at the facility remains contingent upon securing additional financing or strategic partnerships.

Webcast Information

Company management will host a conference call and webcast on November 9, 2026, at 4:00 p.m. Central Time, to discuss the Company's financial results. The live webcast and accompanying slide presentation will be accessible from the Events & Presentations section of Microvast’s investor relations website ( https://ir.microvast.com/events-presentations/events ). A replay will be available following the conclusion of the event.

About Microvast

Microvast strives to be a global leader in advanced battery technologies, with a portfolio of more than 890 patents. Founded in Texas in 2006 and headquartered in Houston, the company has spent two decades engineering cutting-edge battery systems that are intended to power a cleaner future.

For more information, please visit www.microvast.com or follow us on LinkedIn (@microvast).

Non-GAAP adjusted net profit/(loss) per common share is GAAP net profit/(loss) per common share as adjusted for non-cash share-based compensation expense and change in valuation of warrant liability and convertible loan per common share. Non-GAAP EBITDA is defined as net profit/(loss) excluding depreciation and amortization, interest expense, interest income, and income tax expense or benefit. Non-GAAP adjusted EBITDA is defined as net profit/(loss) excluding depreciation and amortization, non-cash settled share-based compensation expense, interest expense, interest income, changes in fair value of our warrant liability and convertible loan and income tax expense or benefit. Non-GAAP adjusted operating expenses is defined as operating expenses excluding non-cash share-based compensation expense. Non-GAAP adjusted gross margin is defined as GAAP gross margin as adjusted for non-cash share-based compensation expense included in cost of revenues.

We use non-GAAP adjusted gross profit, non-GAAP EBITDA, non-GAAP adjusted EBITDA, non-GAAP adjusted operating expenses, non-GAAP adjusted net profit/(loss), non-GAAP adjusted net profit/(loss) per share and non-GAAP adjusted gross margin for financial and operational decision-making and as a means to evaluate period-to-period comparisons. We consider them to be important measures because they help illustrate underlying trends in our business and our historical operating performance on a more consistent basis. We believe that these non-GAAP financial measures, when taken together with their most directly comparable GAAP measures provide meaningful supplemental information regarding our performance by excluding certain items that may not be indicative of our recurring core business operating results.

We believe that both management and investors benefit from referring to these non-GAAP financial measures in assessing our performance and when planning, forecasting, and analyzing future periods. These non-GAAP financial measures also facilitate management’s internal comparisons to our historical performance. We believe these non-GAAP financial measures are useful to investors both because (1) they allow for greater transparency with respect to key metrics used by management in its financial and operational decision-making and (2) they are used by our institutional investors and the analyst community to help them analyze the health of our business. Accordingly, we believe that these non-GAAP financial measures provide useful information to investors and others in understanding and evaluating our operating results in the same manner as our management team and board of directors.

Non-GAAP financial measures have limitations as an analytical tool, and you should not consider them in isolation, or as a substitute for, financial information prepared in accordance with GAAP. For example, our calculation of non-GAAP adjusted EBITDA may differ from similarly titled non-GAAP measures, if any, reported by our peer companies, or our peer companies may use other measures to calculate their financial performance, and therefore our use of non-GAAP adjusted EBITDA may not be directly comparable to similarly titled measures of other companies. The principal limitation of non-GAAP adjusted EBITDA is that it excludes significant expenses and income that are required by GAAP to be recorded in our financial statements. In addition, it is subject to inherent limitations as it reflects the exercise of judgments by management about which expense and income are excluded or included in determining this non-GAAP financial measure. In order to compensate for these limitations, management presents non-GAAP financial measures in connection with GAAP results. In addition, such financial information is unaudited and does not conform to SEC Regulation S-X and as a result, such information may be presented differently in our future filings with the SEC. Changes in the fair value of our warrant liability and convertible loan, which are excluded from non-GAAP adjusted EBITDA and non-GAAP adjusted net profit/(loss), are not expected to recur in future periods, because the public and private warrants issued in connection with the July 23, 2021 business combination with Tuscan Holdings Corp. expired unexercised on July 23, 2026 and the convertible loan was converted and settled on May 28, 2026.

TORONTO, Nov. 09, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- BlackRock Asset Management Canada Limited (“ BlackRock Canada ”), an indirect, wholly-owned subsidiary of BlackRock, Inc. (“ BlackRock ”) (NYSE: BLK), today announced that the iShares Canadian Real Return Bond Index ETF (XRB) (the “ iShares ETF ”) expects to make a special distribution to unitholders in December 2026.

The iShares ETF seeks to provide income by replicating, to the extent possible, the performance of the FTSE Canada Real Return Bond Index, net of expenses. In November 2022, the Government of Canada announced that it would cease issuance of real return bonds immediately, with all existing real return bonds to remain outstanding until maturity.   Accordingly, the proceeds received by the iShares ETF on the maturity of those real return bonds cannot be reinvested in newly issued Government of Canada real return bonds. The special distribution is being made as a result of real return bonds held by the iShares ETF maturing in December 2026.

BlackRock Canada currently expects that the special distribution will represent approximately 14% of the portfolio of the iShares ETF, but this value will vary in relation to the Consumer Price Index (“ CPI ”) and CPI changes. The precise amount of the special distribution per unit will be announced in a separate press release by BlackRock Canada on or about November 18, 2026.

The special distribution will be paid in cash. It will not be paid as a reinvested distribution in additional units of the iShares ETF. Unitholders of record of the iShares ETF at the close of business on December 1, 2026 will receive the special distribution, payable in cash on December 4, 2026.

Information on the tax characterization of the special cash distribution will be posted to CDS Clearing and Depository Services Inc. in accordance with standard industry practice.

NEW YORK, Nov. 09, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Apollo Global Management, Inc. (NYSE: APO) (the “Issuer” and, together with its consolidated subsidiaries, “Apollo”) today announced that it has priced an offering (the “Offering”) of $600 million aggregate principal amount of its 7.550% Fixed-Rate Resettable Junior Subordinated Notes due 2056 (the “notes”).

The notes will be fully and unconditionally guaranteed by certain subsidiaries of the Issuer that are obligors under the Issuer’s outstanding debt securities. The Offering is expected to close on November 13, 2026, subject to the satisfaction of customary closing conditions.

The notes will bear interest at a fixed rate of 7.550% per annum until December 15, 2036 (the “First Reset Date”). On and after the First Reset Date, the interest rate on the notes for each reset period will be equal to the five-year U.S. Treasury rate as of the most recent reset interest rate determination date, plus a spread of 2.672%. Subject to Apollo’s right to defer the payment of interest, interest on the notes will be payable semi-annually in arrears on June 15 and December 15 of each year, commencing on June 15, 2027.

The net proceeds from the Offering will be approximately $594 million, after deducting the underwriting discount but before Offering expenses. Apollo intends to use the proceeds from the Offering for general corporate purposes, including to fund the previously announced investment in Mubadala Capital Asset Management, and to pay related fees and expenses in connection with the Offering and the use of proceeds therefrom.

J.P. Morgan, BofA Securities, Morgan Stanley and Wells Fargo Securities are acting as joint book-running managers for the Offering. Specifically, the Reform of Technical Data and Software Rights to Support Competition, Sustainment, and Readiness (section 861 of H.R. 8800), the Modifications to Technical Data Rights (section 804 of S. 4784), and other provisions related to healthcare and proprietary data.

 Ensuring Patient Access to Critical Breakthrough Products Act of 2025(H.R. 5343 and S.1717) - Legislation to create automatic CMS coverage for devices approved via FDA's breakthrough pathway. (CMS rulemaking for Transitional Coverage of Emerging Technologies (TCET) - advocacy for a new, voluntary Transitional Coverage of Emerging Technologies (TCET) pathway that provides national Medicare coverage for Breakthrough-designated technologies, beginning on the date of FDA market authorization.) The Patient Access to Innovative New Technologies Act (PAINT Act) -- proposed legislation that aims to expand access to new medical technologies by improving the Medicare New Technology Add-on Payment (NTAP) program. It would create a single deadline for products in an alternative pathway, ensure breakthrough devices are eligible for conditional approval under NTAP, and prevent disruption in Medicare beneficiaries' access to new treatments. The Advancing Research for Chronic Pain Act (S. 5041), directs the CDC to regularly collect, analyze, and report data on the prevalence, burden, and impact of chronic pain in the US and build a centralized Chronic Pain Information Hub. The Relief of Chronic Pain Act (S. 3064), which would lower cost-sharing and bar step therapy and prior authorization for non-opioid treatments under Medicare Part D. Starting work on the Food and Drug Omnibus Reform Act of 2026 (Public Law 117-328) - advocacy efforts on Medical Device User Fee Amendments (MDUFA) reauthorization, riders, and device shortages. Reauthorization of the Pandemic and All-Hazards Preparedness Act (PAHPA) (Public Law 109-417) - advocacy on risk mitigation plans and voluntary shortage reporting related to medical device supply chains and advocacy for medical research and to foster a new era of medical innovation and prepare for future pandemics and promote health equity. Support passage of the Radiation Oncology Case Rate (ROCR) Value Based Payment Program Act of 2025 - Senate (S. 1031) & (H.R. 2120). This legislation would increase access to patient care, enhance the quality of cancer treatments, encourage innovation, reduce disparities for rural and underserved patients, and lower patient costs by saving Medicare about $200 million over 10 years. The WISeR Model (Wasteful and Inappropriate Service Reduction Model) - Advocacy efforts on inclusions in CMS' WISeR model, which is aimed at reducing inappropriate care and preventing improper payments under Medicare Part B by refining prior authorization processes for traditional fee-for-service Medicare. Engaged on the Regulatory Alignment for Predictable and Immediate Device (RAPID) coverage pathway and efforts to streamline FDA-CMS coordination and Medicare coverage for Breakthrough Devices. 
 Medical device procurement and supply chain resiliency. Ensuring VHA patient access to Med Tech as VHA manages supply chain and upgrades its medical surgery and prosthetics procurement contracting. Pain management - working to increase veteran access to multidisciplinary and multimodal pain management to provide for effective non-opioid treatment alternatives, specifically H.R.6835. VA Authorization Bill of 2025- Specifically, H.R. 6549 The VA Contracting and Procurement Act. This bill would reform VAs contracting process by modernizing medical implant acquisition and consolidating billing for surgical procedures to enhance delivery of care to veterans. FY2027 Appropriations: Advocacy efforts on including report language in Labor-HHS to advance non-opioid, evidence-based pain management and in VA/DoD accounts to support modernization of procurement processes, including a transparent product add cycle and a streamlined single purchase order mechanism. Take Care of American Veterans Act: Specifically advocating for modernizing the VA's prosthetics and implant procurement program by increasing resources, expanding clinical and procurement expertise, and requiring implementation of a nationwide electronic ordering system.

The Payment Choice Act of 2025 - Summary A bipartisan bill introduced in the Senate and House of Representatives. Its purpose is to ensure that businesses accept cash for on-site sales under $500 and cannot charge cash-paying customers a higher price than those using other payment methods. The bill allows for exceptions, such as a business providing a fee-free device to convert cash to a prepaid card. S. 2326 - Payment Choice Act of 2025 1119th Congress (2025-2026) - Introduced in Senate 07/17/2025 Sponsor: Sen. Cramer, Kevin [R-ND] Committees: Senate - Banking, Housing, Urban Affairs To ensure that United States currency is treated as legal tender to be accepted as payment for purchases of goods and services at brick-and-mortar businesses throughout the United States, and for other purposes. H.R.1138 - Payment Choice Act of 2025 119th Congress (2025-2026) - Introduced in House 02/07/2025 Sponsor: Rep. Rose, John W. [R=TN-6] Committees: House - Financial Affairs This bill requires retail businesses to accept cash as a form of payment for on-site sales of $500 or less and it prohibits them from charging cash-paying customers a higher price compared to customers not paying with cash. Businesses covered by this bill are those engaged in the business of selling or offering goods or services at retail to the public that accept in-person payments at a physical location. The bill establishes exceptions for this requirement, including by allowing a business to provide a device to provide prepaid cards on site for customers to use as payment. Among other requirements, such a card must not have a fee associated with its use and must not require a minimum payment of more than $1. The bill provides for enforcement through preventative relief, damages, and civil penalties.

The Payment Choice Act of 2025 - Summary A bipartisan bill introduced in the Senate and House of Representatives. Its purpose is to ensure that businesses accept cash for on-site sales under $500 and cannot charge cash-paying customers a higher price than those using other payment methods. The bill allows for exceptions, such as a business providing a fee-free device to convert cash to a prepaid card. S. 2326 - Payment Choice Act of 2025 1119th Congress (2025-2026) - Introduced in Senate 07/17/2025 Sponsor: Sen. Cramer, Kevin [R-ND] Committees: Senate - Banking, Housing, Urban Affairs To ensure that United States currency is treated as legal tender to be accepted as payment for purchases of goods and services at brick-and-mortar businesses throughout the United States, and for other purposes. H.R.1138 - Payment Choice Act of 2025 119th Congress (2025-2026) - Introduced in House 02/07/2025 Sponsor: Rep. Rose, John W. [R=TN-6] Committees: House - Financial Affairs This bill requires retail businesses to accept cash as a form of payment for on-site sales of $500 or less and it prohibits them from charging cash-paying customers a higher price compared to customers not paying with cash. Businesses covered by this bill are those engaged in the business of selling or offering goods or services at retail to the public that accept in-person payments at a physical location. The bill establishes exceptions for this requirement, including by allowing a business to provide a device to provide prepaid cards on site for customers to use as payment. Among other requirements, such a card must not have a fee associated with its use and must not require a minimum payment of more than $1. The bill provides for enforcement through preventative relief, damages, and civil penalties.

The Payment Choice Act of 2025 - Summary A bipartisan bill introduced in the Senate and House of Representatives. Its purpose is to ensure that businesses accept cash for on-site sales under $500 and cannot charge cash-paying customers a higher price than those using other payment methods. The bill allows for exceptions, such as a business providing a fee-free device to convert cash to a prepaid card. S. 2326 - Payment Choice Act of 2025 1119th Congress (2025-2026) - Introduced in Senate 07/17/2025 Sponsor: Sen. Cramer, Kevin [R-ND] Committees: Senate - Banking, Housing, Urban Affairs To ensure that United States currency is treated as legal tender to be accepted as payment for purchases of goods and services at brick-and-mortar businesses throughout the United States, and for other purposes. H.R.1138 - Payment Choice Act of 2025 119th Congress (2025-2026) - Introduced in House 02/07/2025 Sponsor: Rep. Rose, John W. [R=TN-6] Committees: House - Financial Affairs This bill requires retail businesses to accept cash as a form of payment for on-site sales of $500 or less and it prohibits them from charging cash-paying customers a higher price compared to customers not paying with cash. Businesses covered by this bill are those engaged in the business of selling or offering goods or services at retail to the public that accept in-person payments at a physical location. The bill establishes exceptions for this requirement, including by allowing a business to provide a device to provide prepaid cards on site for customers to use as payment. Among other requirements, such a card must not have a fee associated with its use and must not require a minimum payment of more than $1. The bill provides for enforcement through preventative relief, damages, and civil penalties.

H.R.1138 - Payment Choice Act of 2025 119th Congress (2025-2026) - Introduced in House 02/07/2025 Sponsor: Rep. Rose, John W. [R=TN-6] Committees: House - Financial Affairs This bill requires retail businesses to accept cash as a form of payment for on-site sales of $500 or less and it prohibits them from charging cash-paying customers a higher price compared to customers not paying with cash. Businesses covered by this bill are those engaged in the business of selling or offering goods or services at retail to the public that accept in-person payments at a physical location. The bill establishes exceptions for this requirement, including by allowing a business to provide a device to provide prepaid cards on site for customers to use as payment. Among other requirements, such a card must not have a fee associated with its use and must not require a minimum payment of more than $1. The bill provides for enforcement through preventative relief, damages, and civil penalties.

Its purpose is to ensure that businesses accept cash for on-site sales under $500 and cannot charge cash-paying customers a higher price than those using other payment methods. The bill allows for exceptions, such as a business providing a fee-free device to convert cash to a prepaid card. Ensuring Patient Access to Critical Breakthrough Products Act of 2025(H.R. 5343 and S.1717) - Legislation to create automatic CMS coverage for devices approved via FDA's breakthrough pathway. (CMS rulemaking for Transitional Coverage of Emerging Technologies (TCET) - advocacy for a new, voluntary Transitional Coverage of Emerging Technologies (TCET) pathway that provides national Medicare coverage for Breakthrough-designated technologies, beginning on the date of FDA market authorization.) The Patient Access to Innovative New Technologies Act (PAINT Act) -- proposed legislation that aims to expand access to new medical technologies by improving the Medicare New Technology Add-on Payment (NTAP) program. It would create a single deadline for products in an alternative pathway, ensure breakthrough devices are eligible for conditional approval under NTAP, and prevent disruption in Medicare beneficiaries' access to new treatments. 2025 Reauthorization of the SUPPORT for Patients and Communities Act - Advocacy for reauthorization of the SUPPORT Act, specifically for FDA approved alternative treatments for Chronic Pain, and medical devices role to address the opioid epidemic. Starting work on the Food and Drug Omnibus Reform Act of 2026 (Public Law 117-328) - advocacy efforts on Medical Device User Fee Amendments (MDUFA) reauthorization, riders, and device shortages. Reauthorization of the Pandemic and All-Hazards Preparedness Act (PAHPA) (Public Law 109-417) - advocacy on risk mitigation plans and voluntary shortage reporting related to medical device supply chains and advocacy for medical research and to foster a new era of medical innovation and prepare for future pandemics and promote health equity. Support passage of the Radiation Oncology Case Rate (ROCR) Value Based Payment Program Act of 2025 - Senate (S. 1031) & (H.R. 2120). This legislation would increase access to patient care, enhance the quality of cancer treatments, encourage innovation, reduce disparities for rural and underserved patients, and lower patient costs by saving Medicare about $200 million over 10 years. The WISeR Model (Wasteful and Inappropriate Service Reduction Model) - Advocacy efforts on inclusions in CMS' WISeR model, which is aimed at reducing inappropriate care and preventing improper payments under Medicare Part B by refining prior authorization processes for traditional fee-for-service Medicare. 
 Medical device procurement and supply chain resiliency. Ensuring VHA patient access to Med Tech as VHA manages supply chain and upgrades its medical surgery and prosthetics procurement contracting. Pain management - working to increase veteran access to multidisciplinary and multimodal pain management to provide for effective non-opioid treatment alternatives. VA Authorization Bill of 2025- Specifically, H.R. 6549 The VA Contracting and Procurement Act. This bill would reform VAs contracting process by modernizing medical implant acquisition and consolidating billing for surgical procedures to enhance delivery of care to veterans. 
 OECD 2 Pillar Framework Implementation - International tax provisions specifically regarding the global minimum tax, including the Defending American Jobs Act (H.R. 591) and the Unfair Tax Prevention Act (H.R.2423), legislation regarding extraterritorial taxation and completion/implementation of the G7 side-by-side agreement. 
 Supply Chain - advocacy efforts on topics that could potentially impact the medical device supply chain such as decisions made by the United States House Select Committee on Strategic Competition between the United States and the Chinese Communist Party, outbound investments, raw materials, components, export controls, and shortage/supply chain resiliency reporting regulations. Submitted comments for the U.S. Dept of Commerce's investigation to determine the effects on the national security of imports of medical equipment including medical devices. Discussed the unique aspects and critical contributions of the U.S. medical technology sector as related to tariffs and other trade measures on imported medical devices and components and our support for policies that do not harm domestic manufacturing and global competition in the sector.

Advocacy efforts include educating lawmakers on the importance of ETO in the sterilization of medical devices and potential shortages of sterile medical devices if EPA's proposed changes are enacted.

The Payment Choice Act of 2025 - Summary A bipartisan bill introduced in the Senate and House of Representatives. Its purpose is to ensure that businesses accept cash for on-site sales under $500 and cannot charge cash-paying customers a higher price than those using other payment methods. The bill allows for exceptions, such as a business providing a fee-free device to convert cash to a prepaid card. S. 2326 - Payment Choice Act of 2025 1119th Congress (2025-2026) - Introduced in Senate 07/17/2025 Sponsor: Sen. Cramer, Kevin [R-ND] Committees: Senate - Banking, Housing, Urban Affairs To ensure that United States currency is treated as legal tender to be accepted as payment for purchases of goods and services at brick-and-mortar businesses throughout the United States, and for other purposes. H.R.1138 - Payment Choice Act of 2025 119th Congress (2025-2026) - Introduced in House 02/07/2025 Sponsor: Rep. Rose, John W. [R=TN-6] Committees: House - Financial Affairs This bill requires retail businesses to accept cash as a form of payment for on-site sales of $500 or less and it prohibits them from charging cash-paying customers a higher price compared to customers not paying with cash. Businesses covered by this bill are those engaged in the business of selling or offering goods or services at retail to the public that accept in-person payments at a physical location. The bill establishes exceptions for this requirement, including by allowing a business to provide a device to provide prepaid cards on site for customers to use as payment. Among other requirements, such a card must not have a fee associated with its use and must not require a minimum payment of more than $1. The bill provides for enforcement through preventative relief, damages, and civil penalties.

Supply Chain - advocacy efforts on topics that could potentially impact the medical device supply chain such as decisions made by the United States House Select Committee on Strategic Competition between the United States and the Chinese Communist Party, outbound investments, raw materials, components, export controls, and shortage/supply chain resiliency reporting regulations. 
 EPA Rulemaking Restricting Ethylene Oxide (ETO) - Proposed rulemaking to place more-stringent limits on emissions and institute new monitoring requirements for ethylene oxide (ETO). Advocacy efforts include educating lawmakers on the importance of ETO in the sterilization of medical devices and potential shortages of sterile medical devices if EPA's proposed changes are enacted. 
 FY2026 National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA) (H.R. 3838/S.2296) - Section 863 of H.R. 3838: Requirement for Contractors to Provide Reasonable Access to Repair Materials If enacted this legislation would enforce an expansive right to repair (RTR) policy on any businesses that contract with the Department of War, mandating that manufacturers provide access to proprietary data and tools. We are engaging in advocacy efforts to have the provision in the House bill removed from the final legislation, and educating lawmakers on the critical role of the Food and Drug Administration in maintaining product safety and effectiveness throughout the device lifecycle in addition to the potential risks associated with third-party servicing of medical technologies. 
 Medical device procurement and supply chain resiliency. Ensuring VHA patient access to Med Tech as VHA manages supply chain and upgrades its medical surgery and prosthetics procurement contracting. Pain management - working to increase veteran access to multidisciplinary and multimodal pain management to provide for effective non-opioid treatment alternatives. VA Authorization Bill of 2025- Specifically provisions to streamline product procurement and the purchase order processes. 
 OECD 2 Pillar Framework Implementation - International tax provisions specifically regarding the global minimum tax, including the Defending American Jobs Act (H.R. 591) and the Unfair Tax Prevention Act (H.R.2423), legislation regarding extraterritorial taxation. H.R. 1990 American Innovation and R&D Competitiveness Act of 2025. To restore immediate tax deductions for research and development (R&D) expenses, reversing the requirement that companies amortize these costs over several years. H.R. 1 (and Senate Amendment 2360) The One Big Beautiful Bill Act- Maintaining the International Tax regime as established in the 2017 TCJA legislation. Policies include proposed changes to GILTI, specifically Country by Country Reporting, the Section 250 deduction, Roundtripping, Section 899, and to return to pre-2022 R&D expensing rules. 
 Ensuring Patient Access to Critical Breakthrough Products Act of 2025(H.R. 5343 and S.1717) - Legislation to create automatic CMS coverage for devices approved via FDA's breakthrough pathway. (CMS rulemaking for Transitional Coverage of Emerging Technologies (TCET) - advocacy for a new, voluntary Transitional Coverage of Emerging Technologies (TCET) pathway that provides national Medicare coverage for Breakthrough-designated technologies, beginning on the date of FDA market authorization.) The Patient Access to Innovative New Technologies Act (PAINT Act) -- proposed legislation that aims to expand access to new medical technologies by improving the Medicare New Technology Add-on Payment (NTAP) program. It would create a single deadline for products in an alternative pathway, ensure breakthrough devices are eligible for conditional approval under NTAP, and prevent disruption in Medicare beneficiaries' access to new treatments. 2025 Reauthorization of the SUPPORT for Patients and Communities Act - Advocacy for reauthorization of the SUPPORT Act, specifically for FDA approved alternative treatments for Chronic Pain, and medical devices role to address the opioid epidemic. Starting work on the Food and Drug Omnibus Reform Act of 2026 (Public Law 117-328) - advocacy efforts on Medical Device User Fee Amendments (MDUFA) reauthorization, riders, and device shortages. Reauthorization of the Pandemic and All-Hazards Preparedness Act (PAHPA) (Public Law 109-417) - advocacy on risk mitigation plans and voluntary shortage reporting related to medical device supply chains and advocacy for medical research and to foster a new era of medical innovation and prepare for future pandemics and promote health equity. Support passage of the Radiation Oncology Case Rate (ROCR) Value Based Payment Program Act of 2025 - Senate (S. 1031) & (H.R. 2120). This legislation would increase access to patient care, enhance the quality of cancer treatments, encourage innovation, reduce disparities for rural and underserved patients, and lower patient costs by saving Medicare about $200 million over 10 years.

Raise awareness of importance of preserving cash as a payment method of choice and facilitate the passage of H.R.1138 - Payment Choice Act of 2025 - for reasons of fairness, resilience and safety. H.R.1138 - Payment Choice Act of 2025 This bill requires retail businesses to accept cash as a form of payment for on-site sales of $500 or less, and it prohibits them from charging cash- paying customers a higher price compared to customers not paying with cash. Businesses covered by this bill are those engaged in the business of selling or offering goods or services at retail to the public that accept in-person payments at a physical location. The bill provides for enforcement through preventative relief, damages, and civil penalties.

patents.Title: quantum computer with improved quantum optimization by exploiting marginal data
patents.Abstract: a quantum optimization system and method for improving performance of variational quantum algorithms using classical post-processing of a measured quantum state. a classical computer estimates, for a quantum state, an expectation value of a hamiltonian based on expectation values of the observables. the hamiltonian may be expressed as a linear combination of the observables. the classical computer transforms one or both of the hamiltonian and the quantum state to reduce the expectation value of the hamiltonian.

patents.Title: cross-merchant promotions
patents.Abstract: in examples, a payment service can identify a first merchant and a second merchant as complementary merchants based on transaction data associated with a plurality of merchants. first transaction data for a first transaction between a first merchant is received, which includes a payment card number. a payment can be processed and apportioned between the first merchant and a second merchant based on an agreement between them. a receipt user interface can be generated that includes representations of the merchants and a promotion for a second transaction between the customer and a second merchant, based on a transaction history of the customer. the payment service can receive second transaction data from the second transaction and process a payment for the second transaction based on the promotion.

patents.Title: multi-participant media control and playback
patents.Abstract: multi-participant media control and playback. in some implementations, a group chat is facilitated among user accounts through messaging application instances executing on user devices. a first request is received via a messaging application instance to commence synchronized playback of media content from a collaborative playlist. synchronized playback of the media content is initiated between messaging application instances associated with the first user account and a second user account. real-time communication is enabled between the user accounts within the group chat while the synchronized playback of the media content is occurring.

patents.Title: optimization of dose distribution in 3d printing by means of a neural network
patents.Abstract: a method of printing a component by using 3d printer, including: inputting a desired dose distribution in terms of the amount of uv light absorbed as a function of location within the component to be printed into a neural network by cad/cam software; calculation of the exposure strategy including the exposure data by means of the neural network, which optimally maps the specified desired dose distribution for the component; and printing the component with the calculated exposure data.

patents.Title: apparatuses, systems, and methods for generating composite displays of oral areas
patents.Abstract: apparatuses, systems, and methods are provided for generating composite displays of oral areas. to generate the composite display, x-ray image data from an x-ray scan of an oral area of an individual and a three-dimensional model generated from a three-dimensional scan of the oral area of the individual are used. the x-ray image is correlated to a rendering generated from the three-dimensional model in the composite display such that structures in the x-ray image are matched to structures in the rendering.

patents.Title: ultrasonic flow meter having flow conditioning arrangements for flow controlling in a linear fluid conduit
patents.Abstract: a fluid flow conditioning apparatus includes a linear fluid conduit having a first tubular body defining a major axis and extending from a conduit inlet to a conduit outlet arranged opposite the conduit inlet, and configured with a predetermined flow geometry to define a linear fluid flow path along the major axis, a fluid inlet non-parallel to the linear fluid flow path, a first fluid flow conditioner configured to receive fluid flow, condition fluid flow, and redirect conditioned fluid flow along the linear fluid flow path along the major axis, a second fluid flow conditioner configured to receive fluid flow from the linear fluid flow path along the major axis, redirect fluid flow away from the linear fluid flow path, and condition fluid flow.

patents.Title: edge termination for power semiconductor devices and related fabrication methods
patents.Abstract: a power semiconductor device includes semiconductor layer structure comprising a semiconductor drift region of a first conductivity type and an edge termination region comprising a plurality of guard rings of a second conductivity type. the guard rings extend into a surface of the semiconductor drift region. the guard rings respectively comprise a first portion adjacent the surface and a second portion spaced from the surface, where the first portion is wider than the second portion. related devices and fabrication methods are also discussed.

patents.Title: semiconductor power devices having multiple gate trenches and methods of forming such devices
patents.Abstract: a semiconductor device includes a semiconductor layer structure and a gate formed in a gate trench in the semiconductor layer structure. the gate trench has a bottom surface comprising a first portion at a first level and a second portion at a second level, different from the first level. a method of forming a semiconductor device includes providing a semiconductor layer structure, etching a first gate trench into the semiconductor layer structure, etching a second gate trench into the semiconductor layer structure, and performing an ion implantation into a bottom surface of the second gate trench. the second gate trench is deeper than the first gate trench, and at least a portion of the second gate trench is connected to the first gate trench.

patents.Title: modular subsurface wastewater treatment system
patents.Abstract: systems, methods, and apparatuses are disclosed relating to onsite subsurface wastewater treatment systems and components thereof. such systems may include a manifold of a subsurface wastewater treatment system. the manifold may further include a front wall and a rear wall, an internal cavity between the front wall and the rear wall, and a length. the manifold may further include one or more conduit port extending from the rear wall, a first connector port configured at one end of the manifold and defining an opening connected to said internal cavity, and a second connector port configured at an opposite end of the manifold and defining an opening connected to said internal cavity. the manifold may be incorporated into a subsystem or system for subsurface treatment of wastewater along with one or more conduits configured to receive and disperse wastewater.

patents.Title: flared end ramp with ribs
patents.Abstract: a flared end ramp for managing and distributing fluid runoff. the flared end ramp may have an inlet end configured to connect to a pipe, a plurality of protrusions on the upper side of the inlet end, and an outlet end. an inclined surface may extend between the inlet end and the outlet end of the flared end ramp, the outlet end of the flared end ramp has a larger width than the inlet end of the flared end ramp such that the inclined surface is angled laterally outward from the inlet end toward the outlet end. the flared end ramp may include a tab positioned on an edge of the outlet end, the tab extending vertically relative to the outlet end. the flared end ramp may be placed inside a stormwater chamber, and the tab may be positioned outside of the stormwater chamber.

patents.Title: wire management system for tonneau cover
patents.Abstract: a foldable panel assembly (e.g., foldable tonneau cover) having first and second panels, the second panel being rotatably attached to the first panel about an axis of rotation. a wire management system is provided including a junction box disposed with the first panel and having an electrical connector. an electrical wire is attached to the electrical connector and extends from the junction box over an interface between the first and second panels. in the extended position, the electrical wire has an amount of slack sufficient to allow the electrical wire to move relative to one or both panels. in the folded position, the amount of slack in the electrical wire is reduced relative to the extended position and the electrical wire is taut over the interface. this configuration permits the panels to be folded and unfolded without pinching or straining the electrical wire during said folding and unfolding.

patents.Title: method and system for assessing internal defects of a material
patents.Abstract: disclosed herein is a method and system for assessing one or more defects in a material. the method comprises extracting one or more assessment parameters from ultrasound waves propagated through a cross-section of the material. further, the method identifies presence of one or more defects in the material by analyzing the one or more assessment parameters using a first machine learning model. further, the method determines a position of each of one or more defects present in the material based on a graphical representation. thereafter, the method determines a severity score and size of each of the one or more defects using a second machine learning model. thus, an improved method and system for assessing one or more defects within a material by generating graphical representations of the one or more defects, thereby enhancing accuracy of defect detection is provided.

patents.Title: combination microwave and hood system
patents.Abstract: a microwave hood system is provided. the microwave hood system includes a microwave oven enclosure defining a cooking cavity therein. a cooking component is positioned within the cooking cavity and configured to emit microwaves. the heating system defines a heating cavity therein, wherein the heating system is coupled to the microwave oven enclosure. a heating element is positioned in the heating cavity. the heating cavity reaches a temperature in a range from about 40° c. to about 80° c. when the heating element is in use. a broiler element is positioned within the heating cavity. the heating cavity reaches a temperature in a range from about hundred and 150° c. to about 300° c. when the broiler element is in use. a dual hood system is also coupled to the microwave hood system.

patents.Title: ventilation control in domestic appliance
patents.Abstract: a cooking appliance includes a wall partitioning a compartment into first and second zones and a housing disposed in the compartment and extending through an opening in the wall such that a first portion of the housing is in the first zone and a second portion of the housing is in the second zone. a flange assembly circumscribes the housing and is disposed against the wall at the opening to inhibit air flow though the opening. the flange assembly has a first member and a second member slidably received in the first member.

patents.Title: laundry machine and corresponding clutch system
patents.Abstract: a laundry machine includes a drum, an agitator, and a clutch. the agitator is disposed within drum. the clutch includes a sleeve and a cam ring. the sleeve is configured to transition between first and second positions to connect and disconnect the agitator to and from the drum, respectively. the sleeve has a first surface. the cam ring is operable to transition the sleeve between the first and second positions, respectively. the cam ring has a second surface and protruding regions extending upward from the second surface. the protruding regions are in engagement with the first surface of the sleeve such that the first surface of the sleeve is spaced-apart from the second surface of the cam ring.

patents.Title: combination microwave and hood system
patents.Abstract: a microwave hood system includes an outer wrapper with a top portion including a cooling air inlet, a cooling air outlet, an outside vent outlet, and a recirculation vent outlet, a first side portion, and a second side portion. a bottom portion includes a vent inlet and is operably coupled to the outer wrapper. a cooking cavity is disposed between the top portion and the bottom portion. a cooking component area is laterally adjacent one of the first side portion and the second side portion. a hood assembly includes a first hood fan disposed between the first side portion and the cooking cavity and a second hood fan disposed between the second side portion and the cooking cavity. a cooling fan is disposed in the cooking component area proximate the second side portion. the cooling fan is in fluid communication with the cooling air inlet.

patents.Title: drying appliance having an accessory port for providing external airflow for powered accessories
patents.Abstract: a laundry appliance includes a processing chamber positioned within a cabinet. a blower delivers process air through an airflow path and through the processing chamber. an accessory port is positioned on an exterior surface of the cabinet and coupled with the airflow path. the accessory port selectively redirects the process air through an accessory airflow path to define accessory process air. an accessory tool that selectively engages the accessory port to define the accessory airflow path.

patents.Title: laundry treating appliance having a wash water treating assembly
patents.Abstract: a laundry treating appliance includes a cabinet defining an interior. a rotatable treating chamber is located within the interior. a liquid recirculation system is fluidly coupled with the rotatable treating chamber. a liquid treating assembly is fluidly coupled with the liquid recirculation system. the liquid treating assembly includes a processing tank at least partially defining a liquid treating chamber configured to receive dirty wash water supplied from the liquid recirculation system for liquid treatment.

patents.Title: hitch sensor assembly
patents.Abstract: a system includes a coupler with a cavity for receiving a coupling member. the system further includes an image sensor coupled to the coupler. the image sensor is configured and positioned to take images of a pattern on the coupling member. the images can be used to estimate a relative orientation of the coupler and the coupling member.

patents.Title: low noise amplifiers with feedback for nanopore applications
patents.Abstract: disclosed herein are devices, systems, and methods that can improve the snr of nanopore measurements by mitigating the effect of parasitic capacitance between the sense electrode and the counter electrode. in some embodiments, a feedback circuit is used to inject a charge into the sense electrode to at least partially cancel the parasitic capacitance between the sense electrode and the counter electrode. in some embodiments, bootstrapping of a signal from the amplifier output or from the sense electrode is used to inject a charge on the counter electrode to substantially cancel the parasitic capacitance.

patents.Title: compositions, kits and methods useful for analyzing antibody-containing samples
patents.Abstract: in some aspects, the present disclosure pertains to sample treatment methods that comprise: contacting an acidic elution solution that is free of primary amine, secondary amine and thiol groups with a sorbent having bound target antibody and separating the elution solution from the sorbent, thereby releasing bound target antibody from the sorbent and forming a first collection fraction that comprises the elution solution and released target antibody; contacting the sorbent with a neutralization buffer solution that is free of primary amine, secondary amine and thiol groups and separating the neutralization buffer solution from the sorbent, thereby forming a second collection fraction that comprises the neutralization buffer solution; and forming a neutralized solution that comprises the first collection fraction and the second collection fraction. in other aspects, the present disclosure pertains to kits for performing such sample treatment methods.

patents.Title: delayed item transaction processing
